correctness.rationale: The checked primary Theorem 6.1 in Micalizzi–Torlo identifies the common endpoint scalar stability polynomial P_p(z)=sum_{j=0}^p z^j/j! for the specified bDeC-family variants on constant linear systems. For Q with d transient pure-birth states and one absorbing state, binomial expansion of the transient block −I+S gives A_{p,k}=h^k/k! P_{p−k}(−h), and the absorbing column equals h^r/(r−1)! G_{p−r,r}(h), G_{m,r}=sum_{j=0}^m(−h)^j/[j!(r+j)]=integral_0^1 t^(r−1)P_m(−ht)dt. Even m factors stay positive; odd m P_m and G_m,r are strictly decreasing to negative infinity and have unique positive zeros. Thus the minimum finite root set is an exact first-and-only positivity horizon for all initial probability rows. Comparison of increasing odd P roots and G_m,r>beta_m proves H_{p,d}=1 for d≥p, p/(p−1) for d=p−1 and beta_3 for d=p−2, p≥3. Fixed d asymptotics follow via the exact Taylor integral remainder, endpoint Laplace estimate and Stirling: W_0(e^(−1)) except d=1 even orders with e^(−1). Independent rational arithmetic verified 3276 entries for p=2..8, d=1..8, h∈{1/3,4/3,11/5}; it is not substituted for the infinite asymptotics.
residual_risks: The theorem concerns endpoint nonnegativity for all rows of equal-rate pure-birth generators, not intermediate bDeC stages or variable-rate/general Markov generators.
The high-order limit keeps d fixed; jointly increasing p,d was not established by the proof.

value.rationale: The exact Markov-chain positivity window is a natural and practically relevant numerical-analysis invariant. It exposes strict separation between all-generator SSP restrictions and finite absorbing-state endpoints, including two sharp finite-size staircase transitions and an unusual even/odd p split for one transient state. It is not merely a reparameterization of a known scalar stability interval.
residual_risks: The result applies to an equal-rate one-way chain and endpoint time stepping; broad high-order positivity for all Markov generators and stages is not established.

limitations: No claims about unequal-rate generators, negative internal stages, floating-point roundoff or p,d jointly growing.
